title: SF3152 (2021-2022 Regular): Minnesota Personal Protection Act amendment

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Minnesota) (gun-policy Stage 5, Minnesota); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Minnesota text (Introduction, 2022-02-11; official copy, https://www.revisor.mn.gov/bills/92/2022/0/SF/3152/versions/0/)
provenance.note: Introduced version as filed (SF 3152, 2021-2022 session, dated 2022-02-11). The quotes join across struck words: Section 3 text reads 'does not expire' after the struck five-year expiry and renewal rules; Section 2 reads 'charge [-a new-] an application processing fee' and is quoted with the struck 'a new' left out. The bill strikes the 90-day renewal window, renewal fee ($75) and late fee rules.

operative_text:
Section 3 (Minn. Stat. 624.714, subd. 7): A permit to carry a pistol issued under this section does not expire and permit cards issued after August 1, 2022, must prominently state that the permit does not expire.
Section 2 (Minn. Stat. 624.714, subd. 3): The sheriff may charge an application processing fee in an amount not to exceed the actual and reasonable direct cost of processing the application or $100, whichever is less.
Section 5 (replacement permits to carry): A person with a valid permit to carry a handgun issued under Minnesota Statutes, section 624.714, prior to August 1, 2022, shall request a replacement permit card that conforms with the requirements of Minnesota Statutes, section 624.714, subdivision 7, paragraph (c), prior to the expiration date listed on the permit holder's card. The issuing sheriff may charge up to $10 to issue a replacement card under this section.
